title: The Cost of Bunkers, Do Owners Care?
section_path: The Cost of Bunkers, Do Owners Care?
section_path_text: The Cost of Bunkers, Do Owners Care?
summary: The Cost of Bunkers, Do Owners Care? The cost of bunkers is a major component of an owner's voyage expense. In paying for the bunkers, the owner is creating a source of revenue for oil companies.

children.title: WS Rate for VLCCs Trading AG/East
section_path: WS Rate for VLCCs Trading AG/East
children.section_path_text: WS Rate for VLCCs Trading AG/East
children.summary: This freight rate becomes a freight bill to be paid by the oil company once the cargo is delivered. The chart on the next page shows the freight revenue for a single VLCC voyage AG/East and the portion of the freight revenue that represents the bunker cost .

children.title: Bunker Cost
children.summary: Freight Revenue Net of Bunkers The above chart seems to suggest that only a small portion of the freight revenue is related to bunkers. The portion of the bunker cost contained in the freight revenue, shown below, has varied from a low of 6% in November 2004 to a high of 51% in April and August of 2002.

children.title: Portion of Freight Revenue to Pay for Bunkers
section_path: Portion of Freight Revenue to Pay for Bunkers
children.section_path_text: Portion of Freight Revenue to Pay for Bunkers
children.summary: Fluctuations in the portion of freight revenue to cover bunkers reflect changes in bunker prices and in the spot market. Of the two, the latter is much more significant.

children.title: Lest We Forget
children.summary: The record proportion of the bunker cost to the freight revenue was 100%, which occurred during the tanker depression of the 1980s when VLCC freight rates fell to WS17. The hapless owner, after carrying a cargo halfway around the world, was given a check for the freight, which he turned over and endorsed back to the oil company to pay for the bunkers.
